steps.text: When you first open Handy Horology Helper, read the Terms of Service and scroll to the bottom.
Then tap Privacy Policy, and scroll that to the bottom too.
Tap I Accept & Continue.
A short welcome shows what you can do. Tap Continue.
Pick how you want to start. Tap Start with my own piece.
Identify opens, ready for your first piece. The tabs at the bottom take you to Home, My Museum, Tools, and Settings.
To change the language, tap Settings.
Scroll down and tap Language.
Pick a language. Each one is shown in its own words, like Español for Spanish.
The whole app switches right away. To switch back, pick English.
Back in English.

chapters.title: Identify a watch from a photo

steps.text: To find out about a piece, tap Identify on Home.
Pick what kind of piece it is. Here it's a pocket watch, so tap Pocket Watch.
Tap the dial photo box, then Choose Photo to use a photo you already have. You can also take one with the camera.
Pick the photo.
Tap Identify.
In a moment you have the report: the maker, the model, the grade, and a price range.
Below, fix anything you know is different before you save. Here: Waltham, Model 1908, grade 645, 21 jewels, made in 1913.
Pick the case metal. This one is Gold-filled.
Tap Save with corrections, then Save to Museum.
Tap Open in Museum. The piece is in your museum, with its photo and your estimate.
To add a piece by hand, tap Add piece on Home.
Pick the kind of piece. Here it's a Clock.
Fill in what you know: the maker, the model, and the year it was made.
Pick its condition. This one is Good.
Type what you paid under Purchase price, and what you think it's worth under Your estimate.
Tap Save to Museum. The clock is in your museum.

chapters.title: Find a piece in My Museum

steps.text: Tap My Museum to see every piece you own. The top shows what your museum is worth.
Tap a kind of piece to see only those. Here, Clock.
Tap All to see everything again.
Type in the search box to find a piece by name.
Tap a piece to open it, with its photo, details, and your estimate.
To keep a list of pieces you want, tap My Museum, then Wish.
Tap Add wish.
Tap Add wish again to open the form.
Type the maker and the model you're after.
Pick the type and how much you want it, then type the most you'd pay.
Tap Save. The piece is on your wish list, with your budget.
To log what you wore today, tap What I Wore on Home.
Tap the piece you wore.
Pick the occasion. Here, Formal.
Pick how long. Here, Full day.
Tap Log today’s wear. It shows up in your wear history.
To share a piece, open it in My Museum.
Scroll down and tap Share.
Tap Share image for a picture card, or Share PDF for a document.
Pick where to send it.

chapters.title: See what your museum is worth

steps.text: To see what your museum is worth, tap Tools, then Museum Value.
The top shows the total value and how it changed.
Tap 1Y to see the whole year.
Scroll down to see value by maker, and your most and least valuable pieces.

chapters.title: Get help with a clock that stopped

steps.text: When a clock acts up, tap Clock Repair Help on Home.
Pick what's wrong. Here, the clock Won't run / keeps stopping.
You get what to try first, step by step, before you buy any parts.
To work out a pendulum, tap Tools, then Pendulum Calculator.
Type the pendulum's length in centimeters. Here, 25.
The beats per minute and per hour show right away, with the nearest common rate.
Or tap a common rate to see the length it needs.
To set a moon-phase dial, tap Tools, then Moon Phase.
You see today's moon, how much of it is lit, and its age in days.
Scroll down for every phase of the month, and a tip for setting a clock's moon dial.
To check a striking clock, tap Tools, then Strike Count Helper.
Type the hour the clock shows. Here, 9.
You see how many times it should strike on the hour, and at the half hour.
